title: Which conflict falls apart, and why the horror stays
highlight: the conflict starts to fall apart
what: The two paragraphs say which conflict falls apart (wanting her, and wanting her to be happy) and why (being wanted is part of wanting her), and the horror now follows from getting past it.
why: Two readers found "the conflict starts to fall apart" skips a step (which conflict, and why), and "But the horror is unavoidable" answers something nobody said.
stays: The test question, the horror, waiting to be wanted, and the pulling-back spiral, in your order.
advice_note: My pick: use it. It reads Human High by itself.
ask_because: meaning: it spells out the reason the old text left to infer ("so if she’d be happier with somebody else, I’d want her less anyway").
old: Most people fail this test: what would I want if she herself thought she’d be happier with somebody else? But if they can get past the initial horror, the conflict starts to fall apart. Being wanted is part of what makes me want someone.

But the horror is unavoidable, because I can’t wait until I know I’m wanted before I let her know I want her. If we both do that, nothing gets started. And it doesn’t stop being true once we’re together. If I start feeling less wanted, I may pull back. She feels me pulling back and starts feeling less wanted herself, then she pulls back too.
new: Most people fail this test: what would I want if she herself thought she’d be happier with somebody else? The first reaction is horror, but if they can get past it, wanting her and wanting her to be happy stop fighting each other. Being wanted is part of what makes me want someone, so if she’d be happier with somebody else, I’d want her less anyway.

I still have to go through that horror, because I can’t wait until I know I’m wanted before I let her know I want her, and if we both do that, nothing gets started. Once we’re together I still can’t wait to be sure I’m wanted. If I start feeling less wanted, I may pull back, and she feels me pulling back and starts feeling less wanted herself, so she pulls back too.
